newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela severance pay reform bill $8.7 bln - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela severance pay reform bill $8.7 bln - Matos.

text.p: The cost of liquidating Venezuela's old severance pay system among public sector workers is $8.66 billion and paying it will receive the same priority as foreign debt, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
"All government debt has the same importance and legitimacy," Matos told Congress. "We are committed to pay our foreign and internal debts, but also our debts with workers," he said.

Severance pay liabilities were "debts that were hidden, camouflaged, but the country's revenues -- including oil revenues -- have to be equitably distributed," Matos said. The government has previously said it would use last year's windfall from high oil prices to pay down foreign debt, rather than internal debt.
Matos said government payments in 1997 and 1998 for liquidating the much-maligned severance pay system would be 636 billion and 2.2 trillion bolivars ($1.3 billion and $4.6 billion) respectively.
Despite the high payout "we expect a scenario under which revenues will allow us to close this year in fiscal balance ... and no deficit," Matos said.

Matos added that the government was working on ways to smooth the debt's servicing until the year 2002. With presidential elections set for December 1998 Matos added: "we are trying to avoid the situation whereby the debt negatively affects the solvency of future governments."

Under the old severance pay system workers received a lump sum when they ended a job, the amount depending on the number of years worked. Under the proposed new system, currently under discussion in Congress, employees will pay funds into pension accounts annually.

The switch to the new scheme -- which will see the government meet accumulated severance payments over five years with a 25 percent payment this year -- is expected to reduce company costs, increase transparency and improve productivity.
Matos added the total cost of the reform was equivalent to 10.1 percent of Gross Domestic Product and would take the total stock of Venezuelan debt at the close of 1997 to $32 billion.
Total Venezuelan debt in 2002 wil be $15 billion, he said.
